Record actual contributions and revisit expected credit as work changes. This record does not itself determine authorship.

## Contribution records

Record contributor, organization or affiliation, project role, contribution description, related data/code/analysis/validation/result/output IDs, contribution period, expected recognition, discussion status, contributor confirmation, and review date. Keep unresolved credit questions visible.

The [contribution and credit template](../../templates/contribution-and-credit-record-template.md) is a reusable starting point. A formal record is not required for every temporary collaborator or small exploratory project.

## Credit and authorship

Discuss authorship or ordered credit early and revisit it as contributions change. Requirements vary by discipline, journal, institution, funder, community, and product. Do not infer authorship or author order from a role title, a single contribution, or the use of the optional CRediT vocabulary.

CRediT can describe contribution types, but it does not determine authorship. Applicable institutional, contractual, journal, funder, community, and legal requirements take precedence.

## Changes and disputes

Record the date, change or dispute, affected contributors, rationale or positions, decision authority, resolution or unresolved state, and effect on communication readiness. Do not make a copied record appear agreed, confirmed, or approved.
